summary: P3E21 explicit bounded route or shared-publication bootstrap with independent source-generation health and no implicit session restoration.
admission: POST /api/v1/session-bootstrap accepts only exact v2 fields. A selector has exactly kind (route or publication) and id (existing identifier syntax). No legacy route_id member or implicit selector. One to8 members, at least one required; duplicate project/kind/id rejected. Equal route and publication names remain distinct selectors. All project authorizations precede any selector lookup, filesystem access or retrieval, including optional members.
selection: Each member dispatches exactly once to existing route or publication compact Brief with require_current=true and limit4. Publication reads preserve its source route/workspace/host and admitted shared revision. Empty, withdrawn, non-local or changed source bindings return existing typed errors, never local-route fallback. A previously admitted immutable reader may finish under existing withdrawal semantics.
result: shin.session-bootstrap.v2 retains task, ready/context_ready/health_ready, independently observed member results and evidence budgets. Members carry selector rather than ambiguous route_id; source route is in the context provenance. Context and health failures remain separate. Required members run first; optional failures are explicit and do not weaken required admission. No cross-project scoring or index merge.
health: Publication health reads its current head and uses only an existing cached assessment for the selected source generation. Project, source route, workspace, host, profile, route fingerprint, preparation and snapshot must match. A route assessment revision is not compared to publication revision: they belong to independent selection counters. Current generation in the health wrapper identifies the publication revision, while assessment.generation retains its original route revision. Old/missing/expired assessments never become healthy by identity matching. No health scan, preparation or repair is scheduled by bootstrap.
agreement: Bootstrap checks returned context against project and exact selector identity, and checks health against the context project, source route/workspace/host, snapshot, preparation and selection revision, including publication_id when selected. If a shared head changes between evidence and health, context remains identifiable but health_ready=false with an explicit disagreement. Member observations do not form a multi-project transaction or promise that heads remain unchanged after response.
continuity: This is stateless task orientation, not a saved session or execution receipt. checkpoint_restored=false and read_only=true remain explicit. Private server-managed checkpoints, producer-authorized receipts and TTL are the following separate continuity slice; no client assertion is promoted to project authority here.
compatibility: Development bootstrap v1 is replaced, not read or automatically upgraded. Outer Server response and route/publication retrieval contracts remain unchanged. No schema migration, global skill change or stable1.26/consumer cutover.

sources.use: Successive observations may see different committed selections. This API intentionally reports independently observed members rather than asserting a distributed/source-time transaction.
